A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PANGEA study. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual multimodal and text-only evaluations, training-data ablations, qualitative examples, and multilingual OCR experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 2–3, the discussion figures, and appendices, including the relocated OCR experiment.

M1.justification: Both retain the LLaVA-Next/Qwen2-7B-Instruct model and the same instruction-construction pipeline. v2 documents the vision encoder and two-stage training more explicitly, without establishing a changed architecture or algorithm.

E1.justification: The 39-language instruction collection, 14-dataset evaluation suite, and ten-language OCR exploration are retained. Naming LLaVA LCS-558K for alignment pretraining adds implementation documentation without establishing expanded task or language coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding main and appendix result tables retain the same evaluated comparator sets. v2's new related-work dataset comparison table describes dataset attributes rather than adding evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a conflicting reported batch-size setting: Table 1 specifies 128, whereas Section 4.1 still gives 512, as in v1. This is a limited change in reported settings; the PDFs do not establish an actual batch-size switch or rerun. Newly stated metrics and zero-shot evaluation are additional disclosures.

E4.justification: Instruction scaling, English-data proportions, language-specific training proportions, and qualitative success/failure analyses are retained. The OCR exploration and its plot move from Section 5/Figure 8 to Appendix J/Figure 27 without new experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the reported performance. v2 introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Several existing results are revised. The MaXM appendix row changes from English/multilingual 48.6/34.3 to 55.3/53.3, reconciling it with the main table, whose multilingual value changes from 53.2 to 53.3. Main-table xChat changes from 35.6 to 35.8 and the multilingual average from 52.7 to 52.8. Appendix XM100 English changes from 30.8 to 30.4 and MGSM multilingual from 47.3 to 47.4. These are reporting revisions, not demonstrated gains from new experiments.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The existing xChat scoring transformation is retained; added metric labels and training-parameter notation introduce no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction reduces the claimed average English advantage over the best open model from 7.3 to 0.4 points, matching the advantage already shown in v1 Table 1. The multilingual advantage changes from 10.8 to 10.9. The central model, dataset, benchmark, and multilingual-performance contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning cross-lingual transfer, English-data balance, cultural understanding, qualitative failures, and OCR weaknesses are retained. The wrong-language response rationale and OCR discussion are relocated rather than substantively revised.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands the previously brief training description with the CLIP encoder, alignment dataset, trainable components, stage-specific learning rates, and H100 training times in Section 4.1/Table 1. It also documents evaluation metrics, zero-shot evaluation, and per-language training counts in Appendix G. Conversely, the front-page project link and direct evaluation-repository footnotes are removed.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a structured comparison of instruction datasets and citations including MultiInstruct, MiniGPT-4, InstructBLIP, M3IT, and OmniCorpus; CLIP is also newly cited. These additions contextualize the existing multilingual and multicultural positioning without redefining it.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, expands the setup description, adds a language-statistics appendix, and moves the OCR discussion and wrong-language scoring rationale into appendices. The acknowledgments are removed. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds training-configuration, dataset-comparison, and language-distribution tables, and adds a metric column to Figure 4. Figure 2 is relocated and its caption clarified; the OCR plot moves to the appendix. Existing result-table structures and qualitative illustrations are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the overstated English performance margin and reconciles several main-text/appendix result discrepancies, particularly MaXM. Added training and evaluation documentation also improves transparency. These benefits are limited by the new table's unresolved 128-versus-512 batch-size conflict and removal of direct resource links. Overall, reporting becomes more useful and consistent, while the underlying empirical support remains largely unchanged.
